overview.title: Welcome to Safi — land of potters and fortifications
overview.p1: Safi (Asfi), on the Atlantic coast between El Jadida and Essaouira, is Morocco's pottery capital. Its kilns, National Ceramics Museum and potters' quarter make it essential for craft lovers.
overview.p2: The city also retains a rich Portuguese past: the sea castle (Qasr al-Bahr) facing the ocean, the Kechla and a dense medina. The fishing port animates the waterfront, while Lalla Fatna and Cap Beddouza offer nature escapes.
overview.p3: One to three days cover the medina, potters, castle and a beach. Safi remains authentic and less crowded than major tourist destinations.

q1.question: How many days in Safi?
q1.answer: One day covers the castle, medina and potters. Two to three days add the museum, Kechla and a beach or Cap Beddouza.

q2.question: Is Safi interesting beyond pottery?
q2.answer: Yes: Portuguese sea castle, medina, fishing port and Atlantic coast form a complete heritage and maritime ensemble.

q3.question: How to get to Safi?
q3.answer: Bus from Casablanca, Marrakech or El Jadida. Nearest airports: Marrakech (RAK) or Casablanca (CMN), then road transfer.

q4.question: What is the best time?
q4.answer: April to June and September–October offer a good balance. Summer suits the beach but can be windy.
